description: A parasitic skin infection caused by hookworm larvae from animal hosts that migrate within superficial skin.
symptoms: Tingling or prickling at entry site
causes: Hookworm larvae from infected cats, dogs, or other animals
risk_factors: Walking barefoot on contaminated sand or soil
Travel or residence in tropical or subtropical regions

appearance.general: Slightly raised, winding or snake-like itchy tracks that advance over time, commonly on the feet and between toes.

prevention: Wear footwear on potentially contaminated soil or sand.
doctor_discussion_points: Discuss recent travel, barefoot exposure, and contact with sandy or moist soil.
